question:
Let \(S\) be a subset of \(\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 2024\}\) such that the following two conditions hold:

• If \(x\) and \(y\) are distinct elements of \(S,\) then \(|x - y| \gt 2.\)

• If \(x\) and \(y\) are distinct odd elements of \(S,\) then \(|x - y| \gt 6.\)

What is the maximum possible number of elements in \(S?\)
solution:
A block of ten consecutive integers is useful because four selected numbers in such a block would be forced into a very specific pattern.

Suppose four selected numbers in one block are \(x_1<x_2<x_3<x_4\). Each gap is at least \(3\), so
\[
x_4-x_1\ge3+3+3=9.
\]
The entire block has span \(9\), so equality must hold. The selected numbers must occupy positions \(1,4,7,10\) of the block. If the block starts with an odd number, positions \(1\) and \(7\) are odd; if it starts with an even number, positions \(4\) and \(10\) are odd. Either way, two selected odd numbers differ by \(6\), which is forbidden. Thus every block of ten contains at most three elements of \(S\).

Partition \(1,2,\ldots,2020\) into \(202\) disjoint blocks of ten. These contribute at most \(202\cdot3=606\) elements. The final four numbers \(2021,2022,2023,2024\) contribute at most two, since three numbers with gaps at least \(3\) would have span at least \(6\). Therefore
\[
|S|\le606+2=608.
\]

To attain this bound, select all numbers congruent to \(1,4,\) or \(8\) modulo \(10\):
\[
S=\{1,4,8,11,14,18,\ldots,2021,2024\}.
\]
The consecutive gaps repeat \(3,4,3\), so any two selected numbers differ by at least \(3\). The odd selected numbers are exactly those congruent to \(1\) modulo \(10\), so distinct odd elements differ by at least \(10\). Both conditions hold.

There are three selected numbers in each of the first \(202\) blocks, followed by \(2021\) and \(2024\). Hence the maximum is \(\boxed{608}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
